Visit note | 2025-07-05 10:00 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Bushra Shikder, 32, female. Ms. Shikder returns for review and mentions ongoing concerns with weight gain, irregular periods, and extra hair on the face. She is a textile engineer who first noticed these issues after a friend in Shyamoli suggested testing. She takes her current medicines and reports no acute pelvic pain or vision changes. Visit note | 2025-07-05 11:30 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Dipak Mondol, 48, male. Mr. Mondol attends for a scheduled follow-up, explaining that he continues to struggle with being unable to reach behind the back and being unable to raise the arm properly. He works as a restaurant cook, and his shoulder stiffness began gradually after a long illness in Gulshan. He reports that pain has fluctuated but range of motion remains restricted, impacting his work tasks in the kitchen. He has no history of direct shoulder trauma, fever, or night sweats, and denies neck pain radiating down the arm. Comorbidity: none. On examination: shoulder lifts only to 100 degrees with marked restriction in external rotation. There is mild tenderness around the anterior joint capsule, but no local warmth or swelling. Distal neurovascular examination of the upper limb is completely normal. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: chronic follow-up; continue current medicines, no new prescription issued today. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.
